**Finding held: Compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

I have resubmitted rather than "repaired," because on these facts there is no repair that improves our position. The verifier's own narrative confirms every substantive element: absence of any audit right is at least as favourable as the preferred position, the cited paragraphs are consistent with that absence, the near-hits are correctly distinguished, and nothing is actionable.

The only way to make the `audit frequency limited` check pass would be to insert frequency/notice/cost language — which necessarily presupposes an audit clause. Drafting one would hand Garman a verification right over Sparkling that the Agreement does not currently give it. That is a net loss for us and directly contrary to the rule's purpose, so I have not done it, and I have recorded the check as **not applicable, for human override** in the finding itself.

Two points for the reviewer:

- This is the third identical outcome on this rule. The check appears to be a structural false negative for the "clause wholly absent" case — the regex has no anchor to match against. It likely needs a guard so that AUDIT is skipped, not failed, where no audit right is detected.
- Residual watch item: if Garman introduces any verification, usage-reporting or self-certification language during negotiation, insert the preferred parameters into § 3 — once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Garman's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no access to our systems.
